mainEntity.name: Should I build an attached in-law suite or a detached accessory dwelling unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached in-law suite connects directly to your existing house structure, whereas a detached unit—often referred to as an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) or granny flat—stands completely separate on the property. Attached additions make sharing central utilities, heating, and cooling simpler, and they offer easier daily check-ins for aging family members. Detached builds provide superior privacy and noise separation for both households. However, detached options typically require independent utility connections, separate foundation work, and more available yard space. Evaluating your lot layout, local zoning, and family care routines helps determine the better fit.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached suites allow shared utilities and quicker access between family members, while detached units provide greater acoustic privacy and independence but require separate site work.
